title: Fpqc coverings detect openness of subsets
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], I any index type, and g_i : T_i → S an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Let V be a subset of the underlying topological space of S. If g_i^{-1}(V) is open in T_i for every i, then V is open in S.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03N0 proof, affine reduction and openness argument; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03N0

proof.text: Restrict to each affine open of S and base-change the fpqc family. The preimage of the restricted subset in every covering member remains open by continuity. Openness is local on the base, so it suffices to work over Spec R.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-affine-standard-refinement] to the restricted family to choose finitely many affine opens V_j of its members whose coordinate-ring product is faithfully flat over R. The spectrum map for each factor identifies with V_j mapping to Spec R, so the subset has open inverse image along each factor map.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-standard-fpqc-quotient-topology] with these finite coordinate rings and their induced R-algebra structures. Faithful flatness of the product gives the required faithfully flat module structure, so the subset is open over Spec R. The affine opens cover S, so the original subset is open.

mathlib_searches.results: Zariski topology, QuasiCompactCover.of_isOpenMap, reduce_to_affine_global; no fpqc family openness criterion.
Scheme.GlueData.isOpen_iff and quasi-compact/open-immersion results; no fpqc family openness criterion.

Flat.isQuotientMap_of_surjective for a single quasi-compact flat surjection, and the existing StandardFpqcQuotientTopology theorem for finite affine families; neither states the general-family criterion. Project-wide source search found no existing general fpqc openness detection theorem.
